name: Chromasin
description: Chromasin is a cross-modal sensory disruptor that chemically decouples thalamocortical routing, forcing sensory inputs to bleed across modalities. Sound becomes color, touch becomes taste, temperature becomes music. The effect is not metaphorical — users are genuinely processing sensation through the wrong cortical regions.
effects: Full cross-modal synesthesia across all five senses
Music perceived as shifting chromatic landscapes
Emotional states rendered as environmental phenomena — grief as cold rain, joy as gold pressure
Mild euphoria from novel sensory integration
side_effects: Sensory overload in stimulation-rich environments — crowds, clubs, transit hubs can trigger panic cascades
Residual synesthesia lasting days after use — traffic noise tasting of copper
Rare: permanent partial synesthesia in heavy users
Interference with BCI signal routing — navigation and comms may malfunction mid-dose
cultural_context: Chromasin is the drug of Shelf art culture — the painters, the noise musicians, the graffiti collectives that tag the underside of the transit corridors. For people who can't afford BCI-enhanced entertainment, Chroma turns the world into something worth experiencing. Tier 1 rave culture is built around it. The irony that it interferes with BCIs is not lost on its users — many of whom can't afford BCIs anyway.
story_hooks: A Shelf artist collective has produced work under Chromasin that somehow encodes navigable hallucinations — people viewing the murals sober report seeing things, and Helix Biosystems wants to know how
A bad batch of Chromasin has caused permanent full synesthesia in a dozen Shelf residents; Nightshade is suppressing the information and the victims need someone to care
A Tier 4 art critic has developed a secret Chromasin habit and will do anything to keep it from their corporate patrons — including covering up what they witnessed at a gallery opening
